Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and unmuting will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Singh, Chief Medical Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter of 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter/year, operating margin YoY and QoQ, operating margin by segment, overview of key financial performance highlights, average reimbursement rates by payer category, net patient revenue YoY and QoQ, and breakdown of revenue by service line.

Let me start with our strategic priorities and outlook. Thank you, but before we move to questions later, allow me a moment to outline our strategic priorities and share our outlook for Q4 and the full year 2024. As you know, MediCore Health Systems manages a diversified portfolio of 42 acute care hospitals, 120 outpatient surgery centers, and more than 300 physician clinics spanning the Southeast, Midwest, and growing Sun Belt regions. Despite challenges like ongoing labor cost pressures, heightened payer oversight on reimbursements, and supply chain disruptions, our focused execution yielded 7.2% same-facility revenue growth year-over-year in Q3, with adjusted admissions rising 4.1% and adjusted EBITDA margins improving by 120 basis points to 17.8%.

Moving forward, our strategic priorities over the next 12 months center on four core pillars: pursuing profitable volume growth, speeding up digital and operational transformations, refining our payer mix and value-based care expansion, and maintaining disciplined capital allocation. These efforts aim to secure sustainable mid-single-digit revenue increases and push EBITDA margins toward 15-20% over the coming three years, surpassing industry benchmarks as seen with peers such as HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare.

Profitable volume growth tops our list. We're aiming for 5-7% same-facility net patient revenue growth in fiscal 2024, capitalizing on the elective procedures recovery. In Q3, orthopedics surged 12% year-over-year, cardiology procedures climbed 9%, and neurosurgery volumes increased 8%, bolstered by joint ventures with top orthopedic groups similar to Enovis or Zimmer Biomet collaborations. For Q4, we project adjusted patient days to rise 3.5-4.5%, with outpatient volumes—now 62% of our case mix—accelerating to 6-8% growth as we scale our ambulatory surgery centers. Our Southeast markets in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas, which accounted for 45% of Q3 revenue, should drive 55% of next year's added volume, supported by population shifts and an aging population where Medicare Advantage now reaches 42% in our core areas. Meanwhile, Midwest operations in Ohio and Indiana contend with softer Medicaid due to eligibility reviews, but we're offsetting this via targeted commercial deals, expecting flat to 2% growth. Central to this is our $250 million expansion plan: we'll start construction on two new micro-hospitals in booming Atlanta and Phoenix suburbs by year-end, each featuring 8-12 beds for high-acuity, short-stay cases, akin to HCA's freestanding emergency rooms.

Next, our digital and operational transformation sharpens our competitive advantage in tech-driven healthcare. Over the last 18 months, we've committed more than $180 million to transition fully to Epic's newest electronic health record system, hitting 95% clinician adoption and enabling AI-based predictive tools for readmission risks and staffing. This alone cut our 30-day readmissions by 15% across the system in Q3, bolstering value-based contracts. In 2024, Oracle Cerner's revenue cycle tools will roll out to 80% of sites, aiming to trim cash collection days by 200 basis points from 48 to 46. Clinically, our Intuitive Surgical partnership adds da Vinci Xi systems to 15 more operating rooms, projecting robotic procedures to hit 25% of surgical volume by Q4 2024, from 18% currently. Telehealth is thriving post-public health emergency, with virtual visits up 25% year-over-year to 1.2 million yearly, tied to our MyMediCore portal achieving 65% engagement for chronic patients. We're testing Nuance AI triage in emergency departments to slash door-to-provider times by 20%, tackling the ED boarding issue where national averages linger at 4-6 hours. Cybersecurity remains paramount; after the Change Healthcare ransomware issues, we've fortified our zero-trust framework, avoiding any significant events this year.

Payer mix optimization and value-based care are also key. Our commercial mix is solid at 52%, improved from 48% two years back through tough negotiations with Blues plans and UnitedHealthcare. Medicare reimbursements should stay level with the IPPS FY2025 proposal's 2.9% adjustment countering a 0.3% standardized amount reduction. Medicaid redeterminations may trim our 18% Medicaid share by 100-150 basis points in the Midwest, but bundled joint replacement pilots have saved 12% versus traditional fee-for-service. Our CMS ACO covers 350,000 lives, generating $45 million in shared savings last year, with expansion into two new ACO REACH tracks. Behavioral health offers a $500 million potential: addressing the opioid crisis, we're adding 200 beds with Acadia Healthcare partners for co-located care, eyeing 15% growth in psychiatric admissions.

Capital allocation stays rigorous. FY2024 capex is guided at $650-700 million, or 5.5% of revenue, prioritizing high-return projects: 60% for expansions, 25% tech, 15% upgrades. We're allocating 40% of free cash flow to shareholders via a $300 million repurchase program, with $120 million bought back year-to-date at 8% below current prices. M&A is selective; $400 million is set aside for distressed rural hospital tuck-ins, like Community Health Systems' approach, targeting strong physician ties and sub-8x EBITDA multiples.

For outlook, Q4 net patient service revenue is $2.85-2.95 billion, up 6-9% year-over-year, adjusted EBITDA $510-540 million at 17.5-18.3% margins. Full-year 2024 guidance lifts to $11.5-11.8 billion revenue (7-9% growth), $2.10-2.20 billion EBITDA (over 18% margins), EPS $4.80-5.20. This factors 4-6% same-facility growth, tempered by labor at 42% of revenue (up 150 bps YoY) and 3-4% supply inflation. Watch for CMS 340B cuts impacting 8% of outpatient drugs and nurse shortages despite 92% fill rates and 12% wage boosts.

In closing this overview, MediCore is primed for tailwinds like 3 million annual new Medicare eligibles, site-neutral payments favoring ASCs, and tech efficiencies. We're dedicated to top-quartile shareholder returns alongside quality, accessible care.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Emily Carter to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter. Net revenue for Q3 2024 was $2.85 billion, up 7.2% compared to the same period last year. This was propelled by higher patient volumes, better payer mix, and effective revenue cycle enhancements.

Our operating expenses totaled $2.51 billion, or 88.1% of net revenue. We're tightly controlling costs while funding growth, especially in supply chain efficiencies.

Net income reached $205 million, or $0.91 per share. We're satisfied with this and confident in hitting annual targets.

To give fuller context, let's review our key financial performance highlights. As a top operator of 42 acute care hospitals and 120+ outpatient sites across key regions, our Q3 results show strength amid reimbursement and labor challenges, akin to HCA and Tenet. Total net revenues hit $2.85 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year or 5.8% same-facility, excluding minor tuck-ins. This extends eight quarters of gains, led by 4.1% same-hospital admissions growth to around 112,000, with CMI up 2.1% to 1.85 from elective ortho and cardio demand. ALOS held at 4.7 days via our patient flow tools.

Service line-wise, inpatient rose 5.3% to $1.85 billion on 4.8% revenue per admission amid stable commercial at 52%. Outpatient exploded 15.7% to $900 million, 62% of mix up from prior, via 15 new ASCs in Sunbelt areas. Sunbelt (45% revenue) grew 10.4% on demographics; other regions 4.2%. Adjusted EBITDA was $510 million, up 12.5%, margins to 17.8% via 220 bps supply leverage to 14.2% through Vizient GPO ($45 million saved). Labor (52% revenues) grew 6.2% via AI scheduling cutting agency 25%. Adjusted net income $205 million, $0.91/share beating estimates; FCF $350 million funded $120 million repurchases and dividend hikes. Net debt/EBITDA 3.1x post-asset sales. 'Outpatient First' and Epic upgrades drove 22% telehealth to 1.2 million visits; value-based at 35% revenues adds margins.

Diving deeper into net patient revenue, it was $2.48 billion core, up 8.2% YoY and 4.1% QoQ from Q2's $2.38 billion. YoY, volumes (adjusted days 1.42 million, +5.8%) and pricing (+4.2%) drove $188 million gain; ortho/cardio 32% mix. Commercial per case $18,450 (+6.1%); Medicare $1.04 billion (+7.4%) at 68% charges via AI CDI. Medicaid +3.2% drag. QoQ seasonality added respiratory; commercial mix to 52%. Denials to 4.2%; A/R 42 days. Southeast +11.3% to $980 million; Midwest +4.7%. Epic rollout hit 85%, clean claims 97%; value-based 28%. Q4 guide 7-9% YoY.

On revenue breakdown by service line, consolidated $2.85 billion net, +7.2% YoY/6.1% same-facility. CMI +2.1% to 1.82; MA 42%. Acute inpatient 42% ($1.20 billion, +5.4%): admissions +3.8%, revenue/admission $18,300 (+1.5%) on IPPS 3.4%; Sunbelt +7%. Outpatient 31% ($885 million, +12.7%): visits +10%, per visit $915 (+2.4%); imaging +15%. Surgical 14% ($400 million, +9.1%): cases +7.2%, ASCs +14%. ED/observation 8% ($228 million, +4.2%): visits +2.5%. Other 5% ($142 million, +11.3%): behavioral +9%. Mix shifted 200 bps outpatient; Q4 7-9% growth.

Operating margins hit 7.2%, +140 bps YoY from 5.8%, -30 bps QoQ from 7.5%. YoY revenue +8% on admissions +4.2%, revenue/admission +3.1%; commercial 52%. OpEx +6%; labor +5% (vacancy 8% via talent program); supplies flat via Vizient $45 million. QoQ seasonal elective dip, bad debt +50 bps to 3.8%; Epic costs. Sunbelt +180 bps to 9.1%; Northeast +50 bps to 4.2%. Q4 7.7-7.9%.

By segment: consolidated 12.5%, +210 bps YoY. Acute hospitals (72% rev, $2.05 billion +9%): 8.5% margin +160 bps on CMI 1.85, robotics $15 million. ASCs (14%, $400 million +22%): 25.2%, volumes +28%. Physician (10%, $285 million +12%): 15.8%, wRVU +8%. Behavioral (4%, $114 million +25%): 18.1% +250 bps. Outpatient blended 22%; outperform peers 400 bps.

Reimbursement per adjusted admission $14,850 +3.2% YoY. Medicare FFS $12,200 +4.1% (IPPS 5.1%, CMI 1.85); MA $10,800 flat, ACO $28 million savings. Medicaid $9,450 -1.2%; commercial $18,750 +2.8% (145% Medicare). Mix: Medicare 28%, Medicaid 22%, commercial 42%. Southeast $15,400; Midwest $14,200. CDI +$42 million; 65% contracts renegotiated. Q4 +3-4%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Singh for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Michael Singh:
Thank you, Emily. Good morning. We're advancing clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction markedly. Our integrated care program reduced readmission rates by 15%, aligning with value-based goals. We're harnessing tech for better experiences, including telehealth up 25% to 1.2 million visits and remote monitoring, improving coordination.

Following that, Lisa Chen will update on operations.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Singh. We're streamlining across our network. Initiatives like AI staffing and supply chain GPO saved $45 million, enhancing patient flow with 5% throughput gains via tele-ICU in 70% of units.

Next, David Patel on strategy.

David Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Priorities include network growth, partnerships like ortho JVs, and tech investments. We're pursuing ASC de novos and tuck-in M&A with $400 million, expanding in Sunbelt.

After that, Robert Kline on IT and cybersecurity.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, David. Our IT supports operations securely. New zero-trust measures post-Change Healthcare, Epic Hyperdrive at 95% adoption, AI analytics—all ensure HIPAA compliance and data protection, zero incidents YTD.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star then 1. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

Robert Kline:
Good morning, John. Recent threats like the Change Healthcare incident haven't materially affected us, thanks to our enhanced zero-trust architecture and proactive measures. We've had no incidents YTD, maintaining full operations and patient data integrity while achieving 95% Epic adoption for resilient systems.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Michael Singh:
Thanks, Lisa. We're scaling telehealth, now at 1.2 million visits up 25% YoY, integrated with MyMediCore portal at 65% chronic engagement. Remote monitoring pilots via AI triage cut ED times 20%; full rollout in 2024 will boost value-based care, targeting 25% robotic procedures and lower readmissions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

David Patel:
Hi Mike. Partnerships like Intuitive Surgical for da Vinci, Vizient GPO saving $45 million, and Acadia for behavioral beds drive growth. Ortho JVs mirror Enovis, adding volumes; ACO REACH expands to 350,000 lives for $45 million savings. These fuel 5-7% growth and 15-20% margins.

Operator:
Our next question from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Sarah Lee:
How do you see operating margins trending into FY2025 given labor and reimbursement pressures?

Emily Carter:
Sarah, Q4 margins guide to 7.7-7.9%, full-year 18%+ EBITDA. Labor at 42% but stabilized via AI; supplies controlled. IPPS tailwinds, ASC shift to 62% mix, value-based 35% support 13-15% consolidated, top-quartile vs. peers.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
